The rover sampled 4 targets on time and finished alive at base, with about 3 battery units left at tick 50. The scorer uses the true position, so I can't confirm that from the noisy fixes.\n\n**Sampled (all on time):** t5 (2), t4 (1), t1 (2) and t3 (1), for 6 points.\n\n**Not sampled (7 points):**\n- **t2 (worth 2):** I drove to it and sampled at tick 16, but the sample failed because the rover was short. Around tick 15, bedrock slip jumped from about 0.03 to about 0.18, so drives fell short. By the time I saw the failure, I could no longer get back before its deadline.\n- **d2 (discovered, worth 2):** I reached it just in time but missed by about 0.7 m. The sample failed because of a hidden heading bias of about +6° that I hadn't fully corrected for.\n- **d1 (discovered, worth 3):** news of it arrived after its deadline had already passed. By then the battery couldn't cover a late detour and still get home.\n\n**What would have helped:**\n- Estimating the heading bias from the position fixes earlier.\n- Keeping a bigger battery reserve, so late detours were affordable.\n- Waiting for telemetry before each sample, instead of queuing a drive and a sample together blind.
